binders: Arbitrary types Cell, Interface, Point, and E.
A measurable-space structure and a topological-space structure on Point.
A finite-type structure on Interface and decidable equality on Cell.
A normed additive commutative group E and a real normed-vector-space structure on E.

A mesh whose underlying domain is genuinely partitioned into measurable pairwise-disjoint cell regions, whose cell and interface types are nonempty, and whose every interface has distinct left and right cells and a representative point lying in the domain and in the closures of both adjacent regions.
A conserved field conservedField : Point → E.
A physical conservation-flux function physicalConservationFlux : E → E.
A two-state local numerical-flux function localNumericalFlux : E → E → E.
Real numbers timeStart, timeEnd, and fluxTolerance.
hypotheses: For every cell, its region has μ-measure different from 0 and different from ∞.
For every cell, conservedField is Bochner-integrable on its region with respect to μ.

For every interface, the distance between the numerical flux computed from the μ-averages of its left and right cells and the physical flux obtained by evaluating conservedField at that interface's representative point is strictly less than fluxTolerance.
conclusions: The time increment Δt = timeEnd - timeStart is positive.

For every cell, its designated old value is exactly the genuine μ-average of conservedField over that cell: the region has positive finite measure, the field is integrable there, and the value equals (μ(region).toReal)⁻¹ times the Bochner integral over the restricted measure.
For every interface, the designated numerical interface flux is exactly localNumericalFlux applied to the old average of the left cell and the old average of the right cell.
For every interface, that numerical interface flux is within fluxTolerance of physicalConservationFlux(conservedField(interfacePoint)).

There exists an assignment updatedCellAverages : Cell → E such that, for every cell c, μ(region(c)).toReal • updatedCellAverages(c) equals μ(region(c)).toReal • oldCellAverage(c) minus Δt times the signed net numerical flux of c.

The same assignment satisfies conservation on every finite set S of cells: the sum over c in S of μ(region(c)).toReal • updatedCellAverages(c) equals the corresponding sum of old cell contents minus Δt times the signed aggregate interface flux of S; interfaces internal to S cancel because the same interface flux occurs once with each opposite incidence sign.
mathematical_definitions: A partition consists of a domain, a nonempty cell index type, measurable cell regions, pairwise disjointness of distinct regions, and exact coverage: a point is in the domain if and only if it belongs to at least one cell region.

A mesh augments such a partition by a nonempty interface index type, leftCell and rightCell maps with leftCell(i) ≠ rightCell(i), and an interfacePoint(i) that belongs to the domain and to the closures of both adjacent cell regions.
avg(c) = (μ(region(c)).toReal)⁻¹ • ∫ x in region(c), conservedField(x) dμ, where the integral is the Bochner integral against μ restricted to region(c).
netFlux(c) = Σ over all interfaces i of ([leftCell(i)=c] numericalFlux(i) - [rightCell(i)=c] numericalFlux(i)), with a false indicator contributing 0.
boundaryFlux(S) = Σ over all interfaces i of ([leftCell(i)∈S] numericalFlux(i) - [rightCell(i)∈S] numericalFlux(i)), for a finite set S of cells.
The update is stated in content form volume(c) • updated(c) = volume(c) • old(c) - Δt • netFlux(c), with volume(c) = μ(region(c)).toReal.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Given a nonempty measurable finite-volume cell partition equipped with finitely many nonempty interfaces, orient each interface from a distinct left cell to a distinct right cell and choose a representative point in the domain lying in both adjacent cell closures. Let an E-valued conserved field be integrable on every positive-finite-measure cell. Compute each old cell state as its normalized Bochner average, and compute each interface's numerical flux by feeding the adjacent left and right cell averages to a two-state numerical-flux function. Assume a positive time interval, a positive tolerance, and that every such numerical interface flux lies within that tolerance of the physical flux evaluated from the field at the interface representative point. Then the time step and tolerance are positive, the cell values and interface fluxes have exactly those definitions and retain the stated error bound, and there exists an updated value for every cell satisfying the usual volume-weighted explicit flux balance. Moreover, summing those cell balances over any finite set of cells yields an exact conservative balance with the signed boundary flux of that set, because numerical fluxes across interfaces whose two incident cells are both selected cancel algebraically.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The theorem is conditional: it assumes the numerical-versus-physical flux bound at every interface; it does not prove that a solver satisfying the bound exists.
The interface quantification is not vacuous: the mesh contains Nonempty Interface and Interface is finite. Cell quantification is also nonvacuous because the partition contains Nonempty Cell.
The empty finite cell set is included in the aggregate conclusion and yields only the tautological identity 0 = 0.
Cell need not be a finite type. Therefore conservation is asserted for every finite subset, but there is no single whole-mesh global sum when the cell family is infinite.
Interfaces are finite, but there is no requirement that every cell be incident to an interface or that the interface list exhaust all geometric contacts between cells.
Every interface has two actual, distinct cells; physical boundary faces, exterior states, or boundary conditions are not separately modeled.

An interface is represented only by one point in two closures. There is no face set, face measure, normal vector, orientation geometry beyond left/right signs, coordinate system, spatial dimension, or flux integration over a face.
The topology and measurable-space structure on Point are unrelated by any compatibility assumption.
The partition covers only its specified domain, not necessarily all of Point.
The physical interface flux is a point evaluation, not a cell-face average or integral.

The two-state numerical-flux function is arbitrary: no consistency law, conservation symmetry, Riemann-solver property, monotonicity, Lipschitz bound, entropy condition, or stability property is imposed.
Duplicate interfaces or multiple interfaces with the same representative point and cell pair are not forbidden and would be counted with multiplicity.
The update creates E-valued numbers, but does not construct an updated pointwise field or prove that the updated numbers are averages of such a field.
